s0338.literal: When Qin extinguished learning, down to Han only Fu Sheng of Jinan orally transmitted twenty-eight chapters.
s0338.idiomatic: When Qin extinguished learning, by Han times only Fu Sheng of Jinan orally transmitted twenty-eight chapters.

s0341.literal: There was also Commandant of the Guard Xiahou, who received instruction from Zhang Sheng and taught his clansman Shichang; Shichang taught his clansman Sheng, forming the Great Xiahou school.
s0341.idiomatic: There was also Commandant of the Guard Xiahou, who received instruction from Zhang Sheng and taught his clansman Shichang; Shichang taught his clansman Sheng, forming the Great Xiahou school.

s0342.literal: Sheng taught his nephew Jian, who separately formed the Lesser Xiahou school.
s0342.idiomatic: Sheng taught his nephew Jian, who separately formed the Lesser Xiahou school.

s0343.literal: Hence the Ouyang, Great Xiahou, and Lesser Xiahou schools were all established.
s0343.idiomatic: Hence the Ouyang, Great Xiahou, and Lesser Xiahou schools were all established.

s0344.literal: Down to Eastern Han at Luoyang, transmission never ceased, and Ouyang was most flourishing.
s0344.idiomatic: Down to Eastern Han at Luoyang, transmission never ceased, and the Ouyang school was most flourishing.

s0345.literal: At the beginning, in the time of Emperor Wu of Han, King Gong of Lu destroyed Confucius's old residence and obtained books stored by his last descendant Hui; the characters were all ancient script.
s0345.idiomatic: At the beginning, in the time of Emperor Wu of Han, King Gong of Lu destroyed Confucius's old residence and obtained books stored by his last descendant Hui; the characters were all in ancient script.

s0346.literal: Kong Anguo collated them against the modern script and obtained twenty-five chapters.
s0346.idiomatic: Kong Anguo collated them against the modern script and obtained twenty-five chapters.

s0348.literal: Of what Fu Sheng of Jinan recited, five chapters matched.
s0348.idiomatic: Of what Fu Sheng of Jinan recited, five chapters matched.

s0349.literal: Anguo followed the ancient script throughout, opened their chapter sequence, wrote them in clerical ancient characters, and combined them into fifty-eight chapters.
s0349.idiomatic: Anguo followed the ancient script throughout, opened their chapter sequence, wrote them in clerical ancient characters, and combined them into fifty-eight chapters.

s0350.literal: The remaining bamboo slips were confused and could not be read again; all were sent to the government offices.
s0350.idiomatic: The remaining bamboo slips were confused and could not be read again; all were sent to the government offices.

s0351.literal: Anguo also composed a commentary for fifty-eight chapters, but when the witchcraft affair arose, he could not submit it to the throne; he privately transmitted his craft to Commandant Chao; Chao taught Yong Sheng of Jiaodong—this was called the Old Text Documents school, but it was not established at court.
s0351.idiomatic: Anguo also composed a commentary for fifty-eight chapters, but when the witchcraft affair arose, he could not submit it to the throne. He privately transmitted his craft to Commandant Chao; Chao taught Yong Sheng of Jiaodong. This was called the Old Text Documents school, but it was not established at court.

s0353.literal: Yet what was transmitted had only twenty-nine chapters, mixed with modern script, and was not Confucius's old text.
s0353.idiomatic: Yet what was transmitted had only twenty-nine chapters, mixed with modern script, and was not Confucius's old text.

s0354.literal: Beyond this there was absolutely no teacher's explanation.
s0354.idiomatic: Beyond this there was absolutely no teacher's explanation.

s0359.literal: In the Jianwu era of Qi, Yao Fangxing of Wu obtained the book in the market at Daxing and submitted it; compared with the annotations of Ma and Zheng it had twenty-eight more characters, and thus it was first listed in the National University.
s0359.idiomatic: In the Jianwu era of Qi, Yao Fangxing of Wu obtained the book in the market at Daxing and submitted it; compared with the annotations of Ma and Zheng it had twenty-eight more characters, and thus it was first listed in the National University.

s0360.literal: What was lectured on in Liang and Chen included the Kong and Zheng schools; in Qi only Zheng's meaning was transmitted.
s0360.idiomatic: What was lectured on in Liang and Chen included the Kong and Zheng schools; in Qi only Zheng's meaning was transmitted.

s0361.literal: By Sui, Kong and Zheng were both current, but the Zheng school was very weak.
s0361.idiomatic: By Sui, Kong and Zheng were both current, but the Zheng school was very weak.

s0362.literal: Of what else survives, there is no longer any teacher's explanation.
s0362.idiomatic: Of what else survives, there is no longer any teacher's explanation.

s0390.literal: The Liang catalog had five scrolls.
s0390.idiomatic: The Liang catalog listed five scrolls.

s0423.literal: The Liang catalog had three scrolls.
s0423.idiomatic: The Liang catalog listed three scrolls.

s0447.literal: Therefore it is said: "What is in the heart is intent; what is spoken forth is an ode."
s0447.idiomatic: Therefore it is said: "What is in the heart is intent; what is spoken forth is an ode."

s0448.literal: The ancients were pure and customs simple; feelings and intent were not yet confused.
s0448.idiomatic: The ancients were pure and customs simple; feelings and intent were not yet confused.

s0449.literal: Afterward the ruler was honored above and ministers were humble below; face-to-face praise was flattery and eye-to-eye remonstrance was slander, so chanting beauty and ridiculing evil served as satire.
s0449.idiomatic: Afterward the ruler was honored above and ministers were humble below; face-to-face praise was flattery and eye-to-eye remonstrance was slander, so chanting beauty and ridiculing evil served as satire.

s0450.literal: At first they only sang and chanted; later gentlemen set them to strings and pipes to preserve admonition.
s0450.idiomatic: At first they only sang and chanted; later gentlemen set them to strings and pipes to preserve admonition.

s0451.literal: Before Xia and Yin, most odes do not survive.
s0451.idiomatic: Before Xia and Yin, most odes do not survive.

s0452.literal: The Zhou house began with Hou Ji; Duke Liu solidified earlier achievements; Grand King laid the foundation of royal traces; King Wen glorified earlier accomplishments; King Wu conquered and pacified Yin's disorder; King Cheng and the Duke of Zhou transformed until Great Peace—they chanted beautiful virtue, following in succession.
s0452.idiomatic: The Zhou house began with Hou Ji; Duke Liu solidified earlier achievements; Grand King laid the foundation of royal traces; King Wen glorified earlier accomplishments; King Wu conquered and pacified Yin's disorder; King Cheng and the Duke of Zhou transformed until Great Peace—they chanted beautiful virtue, following in succession.

s0453.literal: Under You and Li there was turmoil and collapse; resentment and satire arose together.
s0453.idiomatic: Under You and Li there was turmoil and collapse; resentment and satire arose together.

s0454.literal: Afterward the king's beneficence was exhausted and the odes perished; Grand Master Zhi of Lu arranged and recorded them.
s0454.idiomatic: Afterward the king's beneficence was exhausted and the odes perished; Grand Master Zhi of Lu arranged and recorded them.

s0455.literal: Confucius edited the odes, taking from above the Shang and from below Lu—in all three hundred pieces.
s0455.idiomatic: Confucius edited the odes, taking from above the Shang and from below Lu—in all three hundred pieces.

s0456.literal: Down to Qin, they alone survived as material for recitation and were not destroyed.
s0456.idiomatic: Down to Qin, they alone survived as material for recitation and were not destroyed.

s0460.literal: Down to Later Han, three schools were all established.
s0460.idiomatic: Down to Later Han, three schools were all established.

s0463.literal: Wei Jingzhong of Donghai received instruction from Manqing.
s0463.idiomatic: Wei Jingzhong of Donghai received instruction from Manqing.

s0465.literal: The Preface was created by Zixia; Lord Mao and Jingzhong further refined and enriched it.
s0465.idiomatic: The Preface was created by Zixia; Lord Mao and Jingzhong further refined and enriched it.

s0606.literal: The Liang catalog had four scrolls.
s0606.idiomatic: The Liang catalog listed four scrolls.

s0609.literal: The Liang catalog had three scrolls.
s0609.idiomatic: The Liang catalog listed three scrolls.

s0613.literal: Gentleman of the Ceremonial Section Qiu Jibin of the Masters of Writing: Treatise in fifty-eight scrolls, Discussions in one hundred thirty scrolls, General Summary in six scrolls.
s0613.idiomatic: Gentleman of the Ceremonial Section Qiu Jibin of the Masters of Writing: Treatise in fifty-eight scrolls, Discussions in one hundred thirty scrolls, General Summary in six scrolls.

s0618.literal: The Liang catalog had eleven scrolls.
s0618.idiomatic: The Liang catalog listed eleven scrolls.

s0627.literal: The Liang catalog had twenty scrolls.
s0627.idiomatic: The Liang catalog listed twenty scrolls.

s0666.literal: When the Great Way was already hidden, All-under-Heaven became a family; the earlier kings established norms for husband and wife, father and son, ruler and minister, superior and inferior, close and distant.
s0666.idiomatic: When the Great Way was already hidden, All-under-Heaven became a family; the earlier kings established norms for husband and wife, father and son, ruler and minister, superior and inferior, close and distant.

s0667.literal: Down to the Three Dynasties, additions and subtractions differed.
s0667.idiomatic: Down to the Three Dynasties, additions and subtractions differed.

s0668.literal: When Zhou declined, feudal lords overstepped and transgressed; hating that rites harmed themselves, many were burned and cut away.
s0668.idiomatic: When Zhou declined, feudal lords overstepped and transgressed; hating that rites harmed themselves, many were burned and cut away.

s0669.literal: Already in Confucius's time they could not be complete; by Qin they suddenly perished.
s0669.idiomatic: Already in Confucius's time they could not be complete; by Qin they suddenly perished.

s0670.literal: At the beginning of Han, Gao Tang transmitted seventeen chapters; there was also an old classic from Yanzhong; King Xian of Hejian loved antiquity and learning, gathered what remained from the ashes, obtained and presented them—fifty-six chapters in all, including matters of ritual decorum.
s0670.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han, Gao Tang transmitted seventeen chapters; there was also an old classic from Yanzhong; King Xian of Hejian loved antiquity and learning, gathered what remained from the ashes, obtained and presented them—fifty-six chapters in all, including matters of ritual decorum.

s0672.literal: Only the seventeen chapters of the old classic did not differ from what Gao Tang transmitted, though the characters differed in many places.
s0672.idiomatic: Only the seventeen chapters of the old classic did not differ from what Gao Tang transmitted, though the characters differed in many places.

s0674.literal: Cang taught Dai De of Liang and De's cousin's son Sheng and Qing Pu of Pei—hence there were the Great Dai, Lesser Dai, and Qing schools, all three established.
s0674.idiomatic: Cang taught Dai De of Liang and De's cousin's son Sheng and Qing Pu of Pei—hence there were the Great Dai, Lesser Dai, and Qing schools, all three established.

s0675.literal: In Later Han only Cao Yuan transmitted the Qing school and taught his son Bao.
s0675.idiomatic: In Later Han only Cao Yuan transmitted the Qing school and taught his son Bao.

s0676.literal: Yet though the three schools survived they were all weak; transmission never ceased.
s0676.idiomatic: Yet though the three schools survived they were all weak; transmission never ceased.

s0677.literal: At the end of Han, Zheng Xuan transmitted the Lesser Dai school, then collated it against the old classic, took what was sound in meaning, and annotated it—this was the Zheng school.
s0677.idiomatic: At the end of Han, Zheng Xuan transmitted the Lesser Dai school, then collated it against the old classic, took what was sound in meaning, and annotated it—this was the Zheng school.

s0682.literal: By Wang Mang's time, Liu Xin first established erudites, and it circulated in the world.
s0682.idiomatic: By Wang Mang's time, Liu Xin first established erudites, and it circulated in the world.

s0683.literal: Goushi of Henan and Du Zichun received instruction from Xin and thus taught others.
s0683.idiomatic: Goushi of Henan and Du Zichun received instruction from Xin and thus taught others.

s0685.literal: At the beginning of Han, King Xian of Hejian also obtained one hundred thirty-one chapters recorded by Confucius's disciples and later scholars and presented them; at the time there was also no one who transmitted them.
s0685.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han, King Xian of Hejian also obtained one hundred thirty-one chapters recorded by Confucius's disciples and later scholars and presented them; at the time there was also no one who transmitted them.

s0686.literal: When Liu Xiang collated the classics and records, he found one hundred thirty chapters; Xiang arranged and ordered them.
s0686.idiomatic: When Liu Xiang collated the classics and records, he found one hundred thirty chapters; Xiang arranged and ordered them.

s0690.literal: At the end of Han, Ma Rong transmitted the Lesser Dai school.
s0690.idiomatic: At the end of Han, Ma Rong transmitted the Lesser Dai school.

s0692.literal: Zheng Xuan received instruction from Rong and also annotated it.
s0692.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan received instruction from Rong and also annotated it.

s0742.literal: Music is what the earlier kings used to summon the spirits, harmonize the states, unite the myriad people, put guests at ease, and delight those from afar—it has been so for a long time.
s0742.idiomatic: Music is what the earlier kings used to summon the spirits, harmonize the states, unite the myriad people, put guests at ease, and delight those from afar—it has been so for a long time.

s0744.literal: Afterward it declined, collapsed, and by Qin suddenly perished.
s0744.idiomatic: Afterward it declined, collapsed, and by Qin suddenly perished.

s0745.literal: At the beginning of Han, the Zhi clan though recorded its ringing bells and dancing could not penetrate its meaning.
s0745.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han, the Zhi clan though recorded its ringing bells and dancing could not penetrate its meaning.

s0748.literal: Now what survives in writing is recorded to supplement what is missing from the music chapters.
s0748.idiomatic: Now what survives in writing is recorded to supplement what is missing from the music chapters.

s0859.literal: The Liang catalog had fourteen scrolls.
s0859.idiomatic: The Liang catalog listed fourteen scrolls.

s0884.literal: The Liang catalog had twenty-two scrolls.
s0884.idiomatic: The Liang catalog listed twenty-two scrolls.

s0892.literal: In antiquity when Cheng-Zhou was weak and canonical regulations were lost, Lu because of the Duke of Zhou's merit still preserved surviving institutions.
s0892.idiomatic: In antiquity when Cheng-Zhou was weak and canonical regulations were lost, Lu because of the Duke of Zhou's merit still preserved surviving institutions.

s0893.literal: Confucius, relying on the old histories, trimmed and corrected them—sometimes indirect and forming a pattern to preserve the great order, sometimes writing events directly to show the chief evil.
s0893.idiomatic: Confucius, relying on the old histories, trimmed and corrected them—sometimes indirect and forming a pattern to preserve the great order, sometimes writing events directly to show the chief evil.

s0894.literal: Hence there are cases of seeking a name yet perishing, wishing to cover yet being exposed—rebellious ministers and wicked sons were greatly terrified.
s0894.idiomatic: Hence there are cases of seeking a name yet perishing, wishing to cover yet being exposed—rebellious ministers and wicked sons were greatly terrified.

s0895.literal: What he praised and blamed cannot all be written; all was orally transmitted to disciples.
s0895.idiomatic: What he praised and blamed cannot all be written; all was orally transmitted to disciples.

s0896.literal: When disciples withdrew they differed in doctrine; Zuo Qiuming feared the truth would be lost and therefore composed a commentary for it.
s0896.idiomatic: When disciples withdrew they differed in doctrine; Zuo Qiuming feared the truth would be lost and therefore composed a commentary for it.

s0897.literal: When Qin extinguished learning, oral transmission still survived.
s0897.idiomatic: When Qin extinguished learning, oral transmission still survived.

s0898.literal: At the beginning of Han, the Gongyang, Guliang, Zou, and Jia schools—four in all—were simultaneously current.
s0898.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han, the Gongyang, Guliang, Zou, and Jia schools—four in all—were simultaneously current.

s0899.literal: In the turmoil of Wang Mang, the Zou school had no teacher and the Jia school perished.
s0899.idiomatic: In the turmoil of Wang Mang, the Zou school had no teacher and the Jia school perished.

s0901.literal: Ying Gong taught Meng Qing of Donghai; Meng Qing taught Suimeng of Lu; Suimeng taught Yan Pengzu of Donghai and Yan Anle of Lu.
s0901.idiomatic: Ying Gong taught Meng Qing of Donghai; Meng Qing taught Suimeng of Lu; Suimeng taught Yan Pengzu of Donghai and Yan Anle of Lu.

s0905.literal: By the time of Emperor Wen, Grand Tutor Jia Yi of Liang composed exegesis and taught Gong of Zhao.
s0905.idiomatic: By the time of Emperor Wen, Grand Tutor Jia Yi of Liang composed exegesis and taught Gong of Zhao.

s0906.literal: Afterward Liu Xin supervised collation of classics and records, examined and corrected them, and wished to establish them in the schools, but the Confucian scholars did not respond.
s0906.idiomatic: Afterward Liu Xin supervised collation of classics and records, examined and corrected them, and wished to establish them in the schools, but the Confucian scholars did not respond.

s0907.literal: By the Jianwu era, Director of the Masters of Writing Han Xin requested establishment but it was not carried out.
s0907.idiomatic: By the Jianwu era, Director of the Masters of Writing Han Xin requested establishment but it was not carried out.

s0910.literal: Afterward obstinate Confucian scholars repeatedly debated it at court.
s0910.idiomatic: Afterward obstinate Confucian scholars repeatedly debated it at court.

s0911.literal: When Feng died, it was then abolished.
s0911.idiomatic: When Feng died, it was then abolished.

s0914.literal: Afterward Jia Kui and Fu Qian both composed exegesis.
s0914.idiomatic: Afterward Jia Kui and Fu Qian both composed exegesis.

s0915.literal: By Wei it circulated in the world.
s0915.idiomatic: By Wei it circulated in the world.

s0922.literal: At the end of Liang it was lost; now it is suspected not to be the old text.
s0922.idiomatic: At the end of Liang it was lost; now it is suspected not to be the old text.

s0957.literal: Filial piety is Heaven's norm, Earth's righteousness, and human conduct.
s0957.idiomatic: Filial piety is Heaven's norm, Earth's righteousness, and human conduct.

s0958.literal: From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, though honor and humility differ, in the practice of filial piety the meaning is one.
s0958.idiomatic: From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, though honor and humility differ, in the practice of filial piety the meaning is one.

s0959.literal: The earlier kings relied on it to govern the state, transform All-under-Heaven, and thus could achieve order without severity and completion without austerity.
s0959.idiomatic: The earlier kings relied on it to govern the state, transform All-under-Heaven, and thus could achieve order without severity and completion without austerity.

s0960.literal: This is truly the utmost virtue of living beings and the essential Way of kings.
s0960.idiomatic: This is truly the utmost virtue of living beings and the essential Way of kings.

s0962.literal: When Qin burned books, it was hidden by Yan Zhi of Hejian.
s0962.idiomatic: When Qin burned books, it was hidden by Yan Zhi of Hejian.

s0963.literal: At the beginning of Han, Zhi's son Zhen brought it forth—in all eighteen chapters—and the Chief of the Changsun clan, Erudite Jiang Weng, Director of the Palace Workshop Hou Cang, Remonstrance Grandee Ji Feng, and Marquis Zhang Yu of Anchang all named their schools after it.
s0963.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han, Zhi's son Zhen brought it forth—in all eighteen chapters—and the Chief of the Changsun clan, Erudite Jiang Weng, Director of the Palace Workshop Hou Cang, Remonstrance Grandee Ji Feng, and Marquis Zhang Yu of Anchang all named their schools after it.

s0965.literal: When Liu Xiang supervised collation of classics and records, he compared Yan's text against the ancient script, removed what was redundant and confusing, and fixed it at eighteen chapters.
s0965.idiomatic: When Liu Xiang supervised collation of classics and records, he compared Yan's text against the ancient script, removed what was redundant and confusing, and fixed it at eighteen chapters.

s0966.literal: Zheng Zhong and Ma Rong both annotated it.
s0966.idiomatic: Zheng Zhong and Ma Rong both annotated it.

s0967.literal: There is also a Zheng commentary, transmitted as being by Zheng Xuan; its established meaning differs from Xuan's annotations on his other books, hence it is doubted.
s0967.idiomatic: There is also a Zheng commentary, transmitted as being by Zheng Xuan; its established meaning differs from Xuan's annotations on his other books, hence it is doubted.

s0968.literal: In the Liang dynasty the Anguo and Zheng schools were both listed in the National University, but Anguo's text was lost in the turmoil of Liang.
s0968.idiomatic: In the Liang dynasty the Anguo and Zheng schools were both listed in the National University, but Anguo's text was lost in the turmoil of Liang.

s0969.literal: In Chen and under Zhou and Qi, only the Zheng school was transmitted.
s0969.idiomatic: In Chen and under Zhou and Qi, only the Zheng school was transmitted.

s0971.literal: Xuan ordered its gains and losses, set forth its discussions and subcommentary, and lectured among the people; it gradually reached the court, and afterward an edict was issued establishing it alongside the Zheng school.
s0971.idiomatic: Xuan ordered its gains and losses, set forth its discussions and subcommentary, and lectured among the people; it gradually reached the court, and afterward an edict was issued establishing it alongside the Zheng school.

s0972.literal: Confucian scholars clamored, all saying Xuan had composed it himself and that it was not Confucius's old text; moreover the secret repository had never had the book.
s0972.idiomatic: Confucian scholars clamored, all saying Xuan had composed it himself and that it was not Confucius's old text; moreover the secret repository had never had the book.

s0974.literal: Now it is appended at the end of this section.
s0974.idiomatic: Now it is appended at the end of this section.

s0984.literal: The Liang catalog had ten scrolls.
s0984.idiomatic: The Liang catalog listed ten scrolls.

s1089.literal: After Confucius had arranged the Six Classics and lectured on the banks of the Zhu and Si, he had three thousand disciples, seventy of whom mastered the Way.
s1089.idiomatic: After Confucius had arranged the Six Classics and lectured on the banks of the Zhu and Si, he had three thousand disciples, seventy of whom mastered the Way.

s1090.literal: Their responses to the Master and their private discussions and studies—words in accord with the Way—were sometimes written on their sashes and sometimes pursued without satiety.
s1090.idiomatic: Their responses to the Master and their private discussions and studies—words in accord with the Way—were sometimes written on their sashes and sometimes pursued without satiety.

s1092.literal: At the beginning of Han there were Qi and Lu versions.
s1092.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han there were Qi and Lu versions.

s1093.literal: Those transmitted in Qi had twenty-two chapters; those in Lu had twenty chapters.
s1093.idiomatic: Those transmitted in Qi had twenty-two chapters; those in Lu had twenty chapters.

s1094.literal: In Qi: Wang Ji, Commandant of Changyi; Zong Qi, Director of the Palace Workshop; Gong Yu, Grand Secretary; Wulu Chongzong, Director of the Masters of Writing; Yong Sheng of Jiaodong.
s1094.idiomatic: In Qi: Wang Ji, Commandant of Changyi; Zong Qi, Director of the Palace Workshop; Gong Yu, Grand Secretary; Wulu Chongzong, Director of the Masters of Writing; Yong Sheng of Jiaodong.

s1095.literal: In Lu: Gong Fen, Commandant of Changshan; Xiahou Sheng, Director of the Palace Workshop of Changxin; Lord Wei, Marquis of Jie, father and son; Fu Qing of Lu; Xiao Wangzhi, Former General of the Vanguard; Marquis Zhang Yu of Anchang—all named their schools after it.
s1095.idiomatic: In Lu: Gong Fen, Commandant of Changshan; Xiahou Sheng, Director of the Palace Workshop of Changxin; Lord Wei, Marquis of Jie, father and son; Fu Qing of Lu; Xiao Wangzhi, Former General of the Vanguard; Marquis Zhang Yu of Anchang—all named their schools after it.

s1098.literal: The Zhou and Bao clans composed commentarial glosses; Ma Rong also composed exegesis.
s1098.idiomatic: The Zhou and Bao clans composed commentarial glosses; Ma Rong also composed exegesis.

s1100.literal: Kong Anguo composed a tradition for it.
s1100.idiomatic: Kong Anguo composed a tradition for it.

s1101.literal: At the end of Han, Zheng Xuan took the Marquis Zhang's Discourses as his base, consulted the Qi Discourses and the Old Discourses, and annotated it.
s1101.idiomatic: At the end of Han, Zheng Xuan took the Marquis Zhang's Discourses as his base, consulted the Qi Discourses and the Old Discourses, and annotated the Analects.

s1102.literal: Chen Qun, Minister of Works of Wei, Wang Su, Grand Minister of Ceremonies, and Erudite Zhou Shengli all composed explications of meaning.
s1102.idiomatic: Chen Qun, Minister of Works of Wei, Wang Su, Grand Minister of Ceremonies, and Erudite Zhou Shengli all composed explications of meaning.

s1103.literal: He Yan, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, also composed collected explanations.
s1103.idiomatic: He Yan, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, also composed collected explanations.

s1106.literal: Under Zhou and Qi, the Zheng school alone was established.
s1106.idiomatic: Under Zhou and Qi, the Zheng school alone was established.

s1107.literal: By Sui, He and Zheng were both current; the Zheng school flourished among the people.
s1107.idiomatic: By Sui, He and Zheng were both current; the Zheng school flourished among the people.

s1118.literal: The Liang catalog had ten scrolls.
s1118.idiomatic: The Liang catalog listed ten scrolls.

s1139.literal: Thus when the sage receives the Mandate, he must build on accumulated virtue and repeated achievement, abundant merit and thick benefit, sincerity manifest to Heaven and Earth and grace covering the living—what the myriad things turn toward and what the spirits bless—then there is a response of the Heavenly Mandate.
s1139.idiomatic: Thus when the sage receives the Mandate, he must build on accumulated virtue and repeated achievement, abundant merit and thick benefit, sincerity manifest to Heaven and Earth and grace covering the living—what the myriad things turn toward and what the spirits bless—then there is a response of the Heavenly Mandate.

s1140.literal: Tortoises and dragons bear and carry them, emerging from the River and Luo, to record signs of dynastic change; the principle is obscure and reaches to the spirit-way.
s1140.idiomatic: Tortoises and dragons bear and carry them, emerging from the River and Luo, to record signs of dynastic change; the principle is obscure and reaches to the spirit-way.

s1141.literal: The earlier kings feared they would confuse people and kept them secret without transmitting them.
s1141.idiomatic: The earlier kings feared they would confuse people and kept them secret without transmitting them.

s1142.literal: Expositors also say that after Confucius had arranged the Six Classics to clarify the Way of Heaven and man, knowing later generations could not examine together his intent, he separately established weft texts and prognostications to leave them to posterity.
s1142.idiomatic: Expositors also say that after Confucius had arranged the Six Classics to clarify the Way of Heaven and man, knowing later generations could not examine together his intent, he separately established weft texts and prognostications to leave them to posterity.

s1144.literal: There are also thirty chapters, said to have been expanded by the nine sages from the beginning down to Confucius to broaden the meaning.
s1144.idiomatic: There are also thirty chapters, said to have been expanded by the nine sages from the beginning down to Confucius to broaden the meaning.

s1147.literal: In Han there were the Xi and Yuan schools of exposition.
s1147.idiomatic: In Han there were the Xi and Yuan schools of exposition.

s1149.literal: Song Jun and Zheng Xuan both composed annotations on prognostications and statutes.
s1149.idiomatic: Song Jun and Zheng Xuan both composed annotations on prognostications and statutes.

s1150.literal: Yet their literary phrasing is shallow and vulgar, inverted and erroneous, not resembling the purport of the sages.
s1150.idiomatic: Yet their literary phrasing is shallow and vulgar, inverted and erroneous, not resembling the purport of the sages.

s1151.literal: Transmission suggests that after people of the world fabricated them, some perhaps further altered them—it is not a true record.
s1151.idiomatic: Transmission suggests that after people of the world fabricated them, some perhaps further altered them—it is not a true record.

s1152.literal: It began when Wang Mang loved token-destiny; Emperor Guangwu rose through charts and prognostications, and thus it greatly flourished in the world.
s1152.idiomatic: It began when Wang Mang loved token-destiny; Emperor Guangwu rose through charts and prognostications, and thus it greatly flourished in the world.

s1153.literal: In Han an edict also ordered King Cang of Dongping to correct the commentarial glosses of the Five Classics—all were commanded to follow prognostications.
s1153.idiomatic: In Han an edict also ordered King Cang of Dongping to correct the commentarial glosses of the Five Classics—all were commanded to follow prognostications.

s1154.literal: Vulgar Confucians chased the times and further made it their learning; scrolls and titles grew ever more numerous.
s1154.idiomatic: Vulgar Confucians chased the times and further made it their learning; scrolls and titles grew ever more numerous.

s1155.literal: Those who spoke of the Five Classics all relied on prognostications as their explanation.
s1155.idiomatic: Those who spoke of the Five Classics all relied on prognostications as their explanation.

s1156.literal: Only Kong Anguo, Lord Mao, Wang Huang, Jia Kui, and the like rejected it, transmitting the view that it was delusive and false, disordering the canonical mean.
s1156.idiomatic: Only Kong Anguo, Lord Mao, Wang Huang, Jia Kui, and the like rejected it, transmitting the view that it was delusive and false, disordering the canonical mean.

s1157.literal: Therefore, relying on the ancient script obtained by King Gong of Lu and King Xian of Hejian in Han, they collated and examined it to complete its meaning—this was called "ancient learning."
s1157.idiomatic: Therefore, relying on the ancient script obtained by King Gong of Lu and King Xian of Hejian in Han, they collated and examined it to complete its meaning—this was called "ancient learning."

s1158.literal: Confucian scholars of the age also denounced and destroyed it; in the end it could not be established.
s1158.idiomatic: Confucian scholars of the age also denounced and destroyed it; in the end it could not be established.

s1159.literal: Wang Su of Wei promoted ancient learning to challenge its meaning.
s1159.idiomatic: Wang Su of Wei promoted ancient learning to challenge its meaning.

s1160.literal: Wang Bi and Du Yu followed and clarified it; from this ancient learning was gradually established.
s1160.idiomatic: Wang Bi and Du Yu followed and clarified it; from this ancient learning was gradually established.

s1161.literal: By the Daming era of Song, charts and prognostications were first banned; after the Tianjian era of Liang the prohibition was renewed.
s1161.idiomatic: By the Daming era of Song, charts and prognostications were first banned; after the Tianjian era of Liang the prohibition was renewed.

s1162.literal: When the Founding Emperor received the abdication, the ban was even stricter.
s1162.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor received the abdication, the ban was even stricter.

s1163.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, he sent emissaries in four directions to search books throughout the realm; whatever was connected with prognostications and weft texts was burned; those reported by officials were punished by death.
s1163.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, he sent emissaries in four directions to search books throughout the realm; whatever was connected with prognostications and weft texts was burned; those reported by officials were punished by death.

s1164.literal: From this the learning no longer existed; within the secret repository much was also lost and scattered.
s1164.idiomatic: From this the learning no longer existed; within the secret repository much was also lost and scattered.

s1165.literal: Now what survives in writing is recorded and listed under the Six Classics to preserve variant doctrines.
s1165.idiomatic: Now what survives in writing is recorded and listed under the Six Classics to preserve variant doctrines.

s1309.literal: If names are not correct, speech does not accord; if speech does not accord, affairs are not accomplished.
s1309.idiomatic: If names are not correct, speech does not accord; if speech does not accord, affairs are not accomplished.

s1310.literal: Expositors hold that writing arose from Yellow Emperor's Cang Jie.
s1310.idiomatic: Expositors hold that writing arose from Yellow Emperor's Cang Jie.

s1311.literal: Comparing categories and picturing forms is called wen; form and sound mutually enhancing is called zi; written on bamboo and silk is called shu.
s1311.idiomatic: Comparing categories and picturing forms is called wen; form and sound mutually enhancing is called zi; written on bamboo and silk is called shu.

s1312.literal: Hence there are the six categories: pictographs, phonetic compounds, combined meanings, explanatory transference, loan characters, and indicative forms.
s1312.idiomatic: Hence there are the six categories: pictographs, phonetic compounds, combined meanings, explanatory transference, loan characters, and indicative forms.

s1313.literal: In antiquity boys were shown things without deception; at six they were taught numbers and directional names.
s1313.idiomatic: In antiquity boys were shown things without deception; at six they were taught numbers and directional names.

s1314.literal: At ten they entered elementary school and learned writing and calculation.
s1314.idiomatic: At ten they entered elementary school and learned writing and calculation.

s1315.literal: At twenty they capped and began to study the Way of the earlier kings, and thus could complete their virtue and undertake affairs.
s1315.idiomatic: At twenty they capped and began to study the Way of the earlier kings, and thus could complete their virtue and undertake affairs.

s1316.literal: Yet from Cang Jie down to the beginning of Han, writing underwent five changes: first, ancient script, what Cang Jie created.
s1316.idiomatic: Yet from Cang Jie down to the beginning of Han, writing underwent five changes: first, ancient script, what Cang Jie created.

s1317.literal: Second, large seal script, what Scribe Zhou created in the time of King Xuan of Zhou.
s1317.idiomatic: Second, large seal script, what Scribe Zhou created in the time of King Xuan of Zhou.

s1318.literal: Third, small seal script, what Li Si created in Qin.
s1318.idiomatic: Third, small seal script, what Li Si created in Qin.

s1319.literal: Fourth, clerical script, what Cheng Miao created.
s1319.idiomatic: Fourth, clerical script, what Cheng Miao created.

s1320.literal: Fifth, cursive script, created at the beginning of Han.
s1320.idiomatic: Fifth, cursive script, created at the beginning of Han.

s1321.literal: When Qin abolished ancient script it first used eight styles: large seal, small seal, carved tally, seal impression, insect script, signature script, weapon script, and clerical script.
s1321.idiomatic: When Qin abolished ancient script it first used eight styles: large seal, small seal, carved tally, seal impression, insect script, signature script, weapon script, and clerical script.

s1322.literal: In Han the six styles were used to teach schoolboys: ancient script, odd characters, seal script, clerical script, twisted seal, and bird-and-insect—together with draft script, regular script, suspended needle, hanging dew, flying white, and more than twenty forms, all arising from the six scripts above and changing according to circumstance.
s1322.idiomatic: In Han the six styles were used to teach schoolboys: ancient script, odd characters, seal script, clerical script, twisted seal, and bird-and-insect—together with draft script, regular script, suspended needle, hanging dew, flying white, and more than twenty forms, all arising from the six scripts above and changing according to circumstance.

s1324.literal: Afterward in Later Han Buddhist teaching spread in China and Western Region Kharosthi script was also obtained, able to cover all sounds with fourteen letters—text economical and meaning broad—called Brahmin script; its principle differs from the eight styles and six scripts, and is now appended under forms and styles.
s1324.idiomatic: Afterward in Later Han Buddhist teaching spread in China and Western Region Kharosthi script was also obtained, able to cover all sounds with fourteen letters—text economical and meaning broad—called Brahmin script; its principle differs from the eight styles and six scripts, and is now appended under forms and styles.

s1325.literal: Also when Later Wei first settled the Central Plains, military commands were all in barbarian speech; afterward influenced by Chinese custom, many could not be understood, so the original words were recorded and transmitted for teaching—called the "National Language"—now appended at the end of phonology.
s1325.idiomatic: Also when Later Wei first settled the Central Plains, military commands were all in barbarian speech; afterward influenced by Chinese custom, many could not be understood, so the original words were recorded and transmitted for teaching—called the "National Language"—now appended at the end of phonology.

s1326.literal: Also in Later Han the Seven Classics were carved on stone tablets, all written by Cai Yong.
s1326.idiomatic: Also in Later Han the Seven Classics were carved on stone tablets, all written by Cai Yong.

s1327.literal: In the Zhengshi era of Wei a three-script stone classic was also established; by transmission it was considered the correct characters of the Seven Classics.
s1327.idiomatic: In the Zhengshi era of Wei a three-script stone classic was also established; by transmission it was considered the correct characters of the Seven Classics.

s1328.literal: At the end of Later Wei, when Qi Emperor Shenwu held power, they were moved from Luoyang to the capital at Ye; passing Heyang, the bank collapsed and they sank in the water.
s1328.idiomatic: At the end of Later Wei, when Qi Emperor Shenwu held power, they were moved from Luoyang to the capital at Ye; passing Heyang, the bank collapsed and they sank in the water.

s1329.literal: Of what reached Ye, not even half remained.
s1329.idiomatic: Of what reached Ye, not even half remained.

s1330.literal: In the sixth year of Kaihuang of Sui they were again carried from the capital at Ye into Chang'an and placed in the inner secretariat; it was proposed to repair and compile them and establish them in the National University.
s1330.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kaihuang of Sui they were again carried from the capital at Ye into Chang'an and placed in the inner secretariat; it was proposed to repair and compile them and establish them in the National University.

s1331.literal: Soon afterward Sui fell into disorder and the matter was abandoned; the construction office used them as pillar bases.
s1331.idiomatic: Soon afterward Sui fell into disorder and the matter was abandoned; the construction office used them as pillar bases.

s1332.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, Minister of the Secretariat Wei Zheng first gathered them together—not one in ten survived.
s1332.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenguan, Minister of the Secretariat Wei Zheng first gathered them together—not one in ten survived.

s1333.literal: Rubbing copies transmitted by inheritance still remain in the secret repository, together with the Qin emperor's carved stones, appended to this section to complete elementary learning.
s1333.idiomatic: Rubbing copies transmitted by inheritance still remain in the secret repository, together with the Qin emperor's carved stones, appended to this section to complete elementary learning.

s1334.literal: In all, the Six Arts classics and weft texts: six hundred twenty-seven titles, five thousand three hundred seventy-one scrolls.
s1334.idiomatic: In all, the Six Arts classics and weft texts: six hundred twenty-seven titles, five thousand three hundred seventy-one scrolls.

s1337.literal: If people do not study, they do not know the Way.
s1337.idiomatic: If people do not study, they do not know the Way.

s1338.literal: The gentlemen of antiquity were broadly learned without exhaustion, storing doubts to await questioning: learning did not overstep rank, teaching did not cross gradation;
s1338.idiomatic: The gentlemen of antiquity were broadly learned without exhaustion, storing doubts to await questioning: learning did not overstep rank, teaching did not cross gradation;

s1339.literal: words were concise and easy to understand, the teacher at ease and achievement doubled;
s1339.idiomatic: words were concise and easy to understand, the teacher at ease and achievement doubled;

s1340.literal: they both plowed and nurtured, and in three years completed one art.
s1340.idiomatic: they both plowed and nurtured, and in three years completed one art.

s1341.literal: From the time Confucius died and subtle words ceased, the seventy disciples passed away and the great meaning went astray; scholars lived apart in isolation, each forming a different doctrine.
s1341.idiomatic: From the time Confucius died and subtle words ceased, the seventy disciples passed away and the great meaning went astray. Scholars lived apart in isolation, each forming a different doctrine.

s1342.literal: Down to the Warring States, canonical texts were abandoned; Confucian scholars of the Six Classics could not exhaust their fundamental purport and mostly established minor techniques—a single classic reaching millions of words.
s1342.idiomatic: Down to the Warring States, canonical texts were abandoned; Confucian scholars of the Six Classics could not exhaust their fundamental purport and mostly established minor techniques—a single classic reaching millions of words.

s1343.literal: This caused scholars difficulty in understanding; they recited emptily in question and answer until lips rotted and teeth fell out without knowing benefit.
s1343.idiomatic: This caused scholars difficulty in understanding; they recited emptily in question and answer until lips rotted and teeth fell out without knowing benefit.

s1344.literal: The earlier kings established teaching to guard against human desire; it must be rooted in human affairs and broken at the mean.
s1344.idiomatic: The earlier kings established teaching to guard against human desire; it must be rooted in human affairs and broken at the mean.

s1345.literal: Heaven's command is brief and rarely spoken; principles outside the square were indeed not yet explained.
s1345.idiomatic: Heaven's command is brief and rarely spoken; principles outside the square were indeed not yet explained.

s1346.literal: By Later Han charts and prognostications were favored; in the Jin era abstruse talk was honored—boring through and fabricating, daily multiplying.
s1346.idiomatic: By Later Han charts and prognostications were favored; in the Jin era abstruse talk was honored—boring through and fabricating, daily multiplying.

s1347.literal: The correct canons of earlier kings were mixed with the delusive and false; discussions of great refinement were muddied with unrestrained extravagance.
s1347.idiomatic: The correct canons of earlier kings were mixed with the delusive and false; discussions of great refinement were muddied with unrestrained extravagance.

s1348.literal: Decline reached recent times; departure from the correct grew ever more distant, and there was no longer any method of teacher and precedent.
s1348.idiomatic: Decline reached recent times; departure from the correct grew ever more distant, and there was no longer any method of teacher and precedent.

s1349.literal: Study without understanding in the heart, exclusively honoring ornament and show; pre-fabricating mixed difficulties and posing them as adversarial pairs—thus there arose disputations of trimming corners, opposing sides, mutual following, and other competitive sophistries.
s1349.idiomatic: Study without understanding in the heart, exclusively honoring ornament and show; pre-fabricating mixed difficulties and posing them as adversarial pairs—thus there arose disputations of trimming corners, opposing sides, mutual following, and other competitive sophistries.

s1350.literal: Galloping in verbose speech to disorder canonical order, clamor becoming custom without knowing change—this is the blindness of scholars.
s1350.idiomatic: Galloping in verbose speech to disorder canonical order, clamor becoming custom without knowing change—this is the blindness of scholars.

s1351.literal: Ban Gu listed the Six Arts as nine categories, or with weft texts explaining the classics combined as ten categories.
s1351.idiomatic: Ban Gu listed the Six Arts as nine categories, or with weft texts explaining the classics combined as ten categories.

s0336.literal: The rise of the Documents is said to have begun together with writing.
s0336.idiomatic: The rise of the Documents is said to have begun together with writing.

s0337.literal: Confucius, examining the Documents of the Zhou royal house, obtained the canonical records of the four dynasties Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou; he edited what was good, from Yu above down to Zhou below, making one hundred chapters, which he arranged and ordered.
s0337.idiomatic: Confucius, examining the Documents of the Zhou royal house, obtained the canonical records of the four dynasties Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou. He edited what was good, from Yu above down to Zhou below, making one hundred chapters, which he arranged and ordered.

s0339.literal: Also a woman of Henei obtained the Tai Declaration in one chapter and presented it.
s0339.idiomatic: Also a woman of Henei obtained the Tai Declaration in one chapter and presented it.

s0340.literal: Fu Sheng composed a Tradition of the Documents in forty-one chapters and taught Zhang Sheng of the same commandery; Zhang Sheng taught Ouyang Sheng of Qiancheng; Ouyang Sheng taught Ni Kuan of the same commandery; Kuan taught Ouyang Sheng's son, and it was transmitted for generations down to great-grandson Ouyang Gao—this was called the Ouyang school of the Documents.
s0340.idiomatic: Fu Sheng composed a Tradition of the Documents in forty-one chapters and taught Zhang Sheng of the same commandery; Zhang Sheng taught Ouyang Sheng of Qiancheng; Ouyang Sheng taught Ni Kuan of the same commandery; Kuan taught Ouyang Sheng's son, and it was transmitted for generations down to great-grandson Ouyang Gao—this was called the Ouyang school of the Documents.

s0347.literal: Its Tai Declaration differed from what the woman of Henei presented.
s0347.idiomatic: Its Tai Declaration differed from what the woman of Henei presented.

s0352.literal: In Later Han, Du Lin of Fufeng transmitted the Old Text Documents; Jia Kui of the same commandery composed exegesis for it; Ma Rong composed a tradition; Zheng Xuan also annotated it.
s0352.idiomatic: In Later Han, Du Lin of Fufeng transmitted the Old Text Documents; Jia Kui of the same commandery composed exegesis for it; Ma Rong composed a tradition; Zheng Xuan also annotated it.

s0355.literal: In the Jin era what the secret repository preserved was the text of the Old Text Documents; today there is no one who transmits it.
s0355.idiomatic: In the Jin era what the secret repository preserved was the text of the Old Text Documents; today there is no one who transmits it.

s0356.literal: In the turmoil of Yongjia, the Ouyang and Great and Lesser Xiahou versions of the Documents all perished.
s0356.idiomatic: In the turmoil of Yongjia, the Ouyang and Great and Lesser Xiahou versions of the Documents all perished.

s0357.literal: Of Fu Sheng of Jinan's transmission, only the Treatise on the Five Processes composed by Liu Xiang and his son is the correct method, yet it too contains many contradictions.
s0357.idiomatic: Of Fu Sheng of Jinan's transmission, only the Treatise on the Five Processes composed by Liu Xiang and his son is the correct method, yet it too contains many contradictions.

s0358.literal: By Eastern Jin, Mei Ze, Administrator of Yuzhang, first obtained Anguo's transmission and submitted it; at the time the Canon of Shun in one chapter was still missing.
s0358.idiomatic: By Eastern Jin, Mei Ze, Administrator of Yuzhang, first obtained Anguo's transmission and submitted it; at the time the Canon of Shun in one chapter was still missing.

s0446.literal: The Odes are what guide and express the mind and spirit, singing and chanting feelings and intent.
s0446.idiomatic: The Odes are what guide and express the mind and spirit, singing and chanting feelings and intent.

s0457.literal: At the beginning of Han, Shen Gong of Lu received the Odes from Fuqiu Bo and composed glosses—this was the Lu Odes.
s0457.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han, Shen Gong of Lu received the Odes from Fuqiu Bo and composed glosses—this was the Lu Odes.

s0458.literal: Yuan Gusheng of Qi also transmitted the Odes—this was the Qi Odes.
s0458.idiomatic: Yuan Gusheng of Qi also transmitted the Odes—this was the Qi Odes.

s0459.literal: Han Ying of Yan also transmitted the Odes—this was the Han Odes.
s0459.idiomatic: Han Ying of Yan also transmitted the Odes—this was the Han Odes.

s0461.literal: At the beginning of Han, there was also Mao Chang of Zhao, skilled in the Odes, who claimed transmission from Zixia and composed a Gloss and Tradition—this was the old learning of the Mao Odes, but it was not established at court.
s0461.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han, there was also Mao Chang of Zhao, skilled in the Odes, who claimed transmission from Zixia and composed a Gloss and Tradition—this was the old learning of the Mao Odes, but it was not established at court.

s0462.literal: In Later Han there was Xie Manqing of Jiujiang, skilled in the Mao Odes, who also composed exegesis for it.
s0462.idiomatic: In Later Han there was Xie Manqing of Jiujiang, skilled in the Mao Odes, who also composed exegesis for it.

s0464.literal: Earlier Confucians transmitted by succession called it the Mao Odes.
s0464.idiomatic: Earlier Confucians transmitted by succession called it the Mao Odes.

s0466.literal: Zheng Zhong, Jia Kui, and Ma Rong all composed traditions of the Mao Odes; Zheng Xuan composed the Mao Odes Commentary.
s0466.idiomatic: Zheng Zhong, Jia Kui, and Ma Rong all composed traditions of the Mao Odes; Zheng Xuan composed the Mao Odes Commentary.

s0467.literal: The Qi Odes were already lost in Wei.
s0467.idiomatic: The Qi Odes were already lost in Wei.

s0468.literal: The Lu Odes perished in Western Jin.
s0468.idiomatic: The Lu Odes perished in Western Jin.

s0469.literal: Though the Han Odes survived, there was no one to transmit them.
s0469.idiomatic: Though the Han Odes survived, there was no one to transmit them.

s0470.literal: Only the Zheng Commentary on the Mao Odes stands alone to the present.
s0470.idiomatic: Only the Zheng Commentary on the Mao Odes stands alone to the present.

s0388.literal: 有Mao Odes問難二卷，王肅撰，亡。.
s0388.idiomatic: 有Mao Odes問難二卷，王肅撰，亡。.

s0392.literal: 又Mao Odes釋義十卷，謝沈撰；.
s0392.idiomatic: 又Mao Odes釋義十卷，謝沈撰；.

s0540.literal: 又喪服世要一卷，庾蔚之撰；.
s0540.idiomatic: 又喪服世要一卷，庾蔚之撰；.

s0622.literal: 宋光祿大夫傅隆議二卷，祭法五卷。.
s0622.idiomatic: 宋光祿大夫傅隆議二卷，祭法五卷。.

s0647.literal: 又郊丘議三卷，魏太尉蔣濟撰；.
s0647.idiomatic: 又郊丘議三卷，魏太尉蔣濟撰；.

s0671.literal: 而又得司馬穰苴兵法一百五十五篇，及明堂陰陽之記，並無敢傳之者。.
s0671.idiomatic: 而又得司馬穰苴兵法一百五十五篇，及明堂陰陽之記，並無敢傳之者。.

s0673.literal: 自高堂生至宣帝時後蒼，最明其業，乃為曲台記。.
s0673.idiomatic: 自高堂生至宣帝時後蒼，最明其業，乃為曲台記。.

s0678.literal: 其喪服一篇，子夏先傳之，諸儒多為注解，今又別行。.
s0678.idiomatic: 其喪服一篇，子夏先傳之，諸儒多為注解，今又別行。.

s0680.literal: 周官蓋周公所制官政之法，上于河間獻王，獨闕冬官一篇。.
s0680.idiomatic: 周官蓋周公所制官政之法，上于河間獻王，獨闕冬官一篇。.

s0681.literal: 獻王購以千金不得，遂取考工記以補其處，合成六篇奏之。.
s0681.idiomatic: 獻王購以千金不得，遂取考工記以補其處，合成六篇奏之。.

s0684.literal: 是後馬融作周官傳，以授鄭玄，玄作周官注。.
s0684.idiomatic: 是後馬融作周官傳，以授鄭玄，玄作周官注。.

s0687.literal: 而又得明堂陰陽記三十三篇、孔子三朝記七篇、王史氏記二十一篇、Music記二十三篇，凡五種，合二百十四篇。.
s0687.idiomatic: 而又得明堂陰陽記三十三篇、孔子三朝記七篇、王史氏記二十一篇、Music記二十三篇，凡五種，合二百十四篇。.

s0688.literal: 戴德刪其煩重，合而記之，為八十五篇，謂之大戴記。.
s0688.idiomatic: 戴德刪其煩重，合而記之，為八十五篇，謂之大戴記。.

s0689.literal: 而戴聖又刪大戴之Documents，為四十六篇，謂之小戴記。.
s0689.idiomatic: 而戴聖又刪大戴之Documents，為四十六篇，謂之小戴記。.

s0691.literal: 融又定月令一篇、明堂位一篇、Music記一篇，合四十九篇；.
s0691.idiomatic: 融又定月令一篇、明堂位一篇、Music記一篇，合四十九篇；.

s0693.literal: 今周官六篇、古經十七篇、小戴記四十九篇，凡三種。.
s0693.idiomatic: 今周官六篇、古經十七篇、小戴記四十九篇，凡三種。.

s0694.literal: 唯鄭注立于國學，其餘並多散亡，又無師說。.
s0694.idiomatic: 唯鄭注立于國學，其餘並多散亡，又無師說。.

s0743.literal: 周人存六代之Music，曰雲門、咸池、大韶、大夏、大護、大武。.
s0743.idiomatic: 周人存六代之Music，曰雲門、咸池、大韶、大夏、大護、大武。.

s0746.literal: 其後竇公、河間獻王、常山王、張禹，咸獻MusicDocuments。.
s0746.idiomatic: 其後竇公、河間獻王、常山王、張禹，咸獻MusicDocuments。.

s0747.literal: 魏、晉已後，雖加損益，去正轉遠，事在聲Music志。.
s0747.idiomatic: 魏、晉已後，雖加損益，去正轉遠，事在聲Music志。.

s0749.literal: 春秋春秋經十一卷吳衛將軍士燮注。.
s0749.idiomatic: 春秋春秋經十一卷吳衛將軍士燮注。.

s0758.literal: 春秋杜氏、服氏注春秋左傳十卷殘缺。.
s0758.idiomatic: 春秋杜氏、服氏注春秋左傳十卷殘缺。.

s0807.literal: 劉寔等集解春秋序一卷.
s0807.idiomatic: 劉寔等集解春秋序一卷.

s0828.literal: 春秋公羊音，李軌、晉徵士江淳撰，各一卷。.
s0828.idiomatic: 春秋公羊音，李軌、晉徵士江淳撰，各一卷。.

s0863.literal: 糜信理何氏漢議二卷魏人撰。.
s0863.idiomatic: 糜信理何氏漢議二卷魏人撰。.

s0866.literal: 徐邈答春秋谷梁義三卷.
s0866.idiomatic: 徐邈答春秋谷梁義三卷.

s0867.literal: 薄叔玄問谷梁義二卷梁四卷。.
s0867.idiomatic: 薄叔玄問谷梁義二卷梁四卷。.

s0900.literal: 初，齊人胡母子都傳公羊春秋，授東海嬴公。.
s0900.idiomatic: 初，齊人胡母子都傳公羊春秋，授東海嬴公。.

s0902.literal: 故後漢公羊有嚴氏、顏氏之學，與谷梁三家並立。.
s0902.idiomatic: 故後漢公羊有嚴氏、顏氏之學，與谷梁三家並立。.

s0903.literal: 漢末，何休又作公羊解說。.
s0903.idiomatic: 漢末，何休又作公羊解說。.

s0904.literal: 而左氏漢初出於張蒼之家，本無傳者。.
s0904.idiomatic: 而左氏漢初出於張蒼之家，本無傳者。.

s0908.literal: 時陳元最明左傳，又上Documents訟之。.
s0908.idiomatic: 時陳元最明左傳，又上Documents訟之。.

s0909.literal: 於是乃以魏郡李封為左氏博士。.
s0909.idiomatic: 於是乃以魏郡李封為左氏博士。.

s0913.literal: 永平中，能為左氏者，擢高第為講郎。.
s0913.idiomatic: 永平中，能為左氏者，擢高第為講郎。.

s0916.literal: 晉時，杜預又為經傳集解。.
s0916.idiomatic: 晉時，杜預又為經傳集解。.

s0917.literal: 谷梁範甯注、公羊何休注、左氏服虔、杜預注，俱立國學。.
s0917.idiomatic: 谷梁範甯注、公羊何休注、左氏服虔、杜預注，俱立國學。.

s0918.literal: 然公羊、谷梁，但試讀文，而不能通其義。.
s0918.idiomatic: 然公羊、谷梁，但試讀文，而不能通其義。.

s0919.literal: 後學三傳通講，而左氏唯傳服義。.
s0919.idiomatic: 後學三傳通講，而左氏唯傳服義。.

s0920.literal: 至隋，杜氏盛行，服義及公羊、谷梁浸微，今殆無師說。.
s0920.idiomatic: 至隋，杜氏盛行，服義及公羊、谷梁浸微，今殆無師說。.

s0921.literal: 孝經古文孝經一卷孔安國傳。.
s0921.idiomatic: 孝經古文孝經一卷孔安國傳。.

s0933.literal: 又有晉給事中楊泓，處士虞槃佐、孫氏，東陽太守殷仲文，晉陵太守殷叔道，丹陽尹車胤，孔光各注孝經一卷；.
s0933.idiomatic: 又有晉給事中楊泓，處士虞槃佐、孫氏，東陽太守殷仲文，晉陵太守殷叔道，丹陽尹車胤，孔光各注孝經一卷；.

s0935.literal: 宋何承天、費沈，齊光祿大夫王玄載，國子博士明僧紹，梁五經博士嚴植之，Documents功論郎曹思文，羽林監江系之，江遜等注孝經各一卷；.
s0935.idiomatic: 宋何承天、費沈，齊光祿大夫王玄載，國子博士明僧紹，梁五經博士嚴植之，Documents功論郎曹思文，羽林監江系之，江遜等注孝經各一卷；.

s0961.literal: 孔子既敘六經，題目不同，指意差別，恐斯道離散，故作孝經，以總會之，明其枝流雖分，本萌於孝者也。.
s0961.idiomatic: 孔子既敘六經，題目不同，指意差別，恐斯道離散，故作孝經，以總會之，明其枝流雖分，本萌於孝者也。.

s0970.literal: 至隋，秘Documents監王劭于京師訪得孔傳，送至河間劉炫。.
s0970.idiomatic: 至隋，秘Documents監王劭于京師訪得孔傳，送至河間劉炫。.

s0973.literal: 又雲魏氏遷洛，未達華語，孝文帝命侯伏侯可悉陵，以夷言譯孝經之旨，教於國人，謂之國語孝經。.
s0973.idiomatic: 又雲魏氏遷洛，未達華語，孝文帝命侯伏侯可悉陵，以夷言譯孝經之旨，教於國人，謂之國語孝經。.

s0977.literal: 又王肅、虞翻、譙周等注論語各十卷。.
s0977.idiomatic: 又王肅、虞翻、譙周等注論語各十卷。.

s0991.literal: 又論語音二卷，徐邈等撰。.
s0991.idiomatic: 又論語音二卷，徐邈等撰。.

s1014.literal: 又蔡系論語釋一卷，張隱論語釋一卷，郤原通鄭一卷，王氏修鄭錯一卷，薑處道論釋一卷。.
s1014.idiomatic: 又蔡系論語釋一卷，張隱論語釋一卷，郤原通鄭一卷，王氏修鄭錯一卷，薑處道論釋一卷。.

s1091.literal: 仲尼既沒，遂緝而論之，謂之論語。.
s1091.idiomatic: 仲尼既沒，遂緝而論之，謂之論語。.

s1096.literal: 張禹本授魯論，晚講齊論，後遂合而考之，刪其煩惑。.
s1096.idiomatic: 張禹本授魯論，晚講齊論，後遂合而考之，刪其煩惑。.

s1097.literal: 除去齊論·問王、知道二篇，從魯論二十篇為定，號張侯論，當世重之。.
s1097.idiomatic: 除去齊論·問王、知道二篇，從魯論二十篇為定，號張侯論，當世重之。.

s1099.literal: 又有古論語，與Old Text Documents同出，章句煩省，與魯論不異，唯分子張為二篇，故有二十一篇。.
s1099.idiomatic: 又有古論語，與Old Text Documents同出，章句煩省，與魯論不異，唯分子張為二篇，故有二十一篇。.

s1104.literal: 是後諸儒多為之注，齊論遂亡。.
s1104.idiomatic: 是後諸儒多為之注，齊論遂亡。.

s1105.literal: 古論先無師說，梁、陳之時，唯鄭玄、何晏立于國學，而鄭氏甚微。.
s1105.idiomatic: 古論先無師說，梁、陳之時，唯鄭玄、何晏立于國學，而鄭氏甚微。.

s1108.literal: 其孔叢、家語，並孔氏所傳仲尼之旨。.
s1108.idiomatic: 其孔叢、家語，並孔氏所傳仲尼之旨。.

s1109.literal: 爾雅諸Documents，解古今之意，並五經總義，附於此篇。.
s1109.idiomatic: 爾雅諸Documents，解古今之意，並五經總義，附於此篇。.

s1110.literal: 經緯河圖二十卷梁河圖洛Documents二十四卷，目錄一卷，亡。.
s1110.idiomatic: 經緯河圖二十卷梁河圖洛Documents二十四卷，目錄一卷，亡。.

s1127.literal: 春秋內事四卷，春秋包命二卷，春秋秘事十一卷，Documents、易、Odes、孝經、春秋、河洛緯秘要一卷，五帝鉤命訣圖一卷。.
s1127.idiomatic: 春秋內事四卷，春秋包命二卷，春秋秘事十一卷，Documents、易、Odes、孝經、春秋、河洛緯秘要一卷，五帝鉤命訣圖一卷。.

s1132.literal: 孝經元命包一卷，孝經古秘援神二卷，孝經古秘圖一卷，孝經左右握二卷，孝經左右契圖一卷，孝經雌雄圖三卷，孝經異本雌雄圖二卷，孝經分野圖一卷，孝經內事圖二卷，孝經內事星宿講堂七十二弟子圖一卷，又口授圖一卷；.
s1132.idiomatic: 孝經元命包一卷，孝經古秘援神二卷，孝經古秘圖一卷，孝經左右握二卷，孝經左右契圖一卷，孝經雌雄圖三卷，孝經異本雌雄圖二卷，孝經分野圖一卷，孝經內事圖二卷，孝經內事星宿講堂七十二弟子圖一卷，又口授圖一卷；.

s1134.literal: 孔老讖十二卷，老子河洛讖一卷，尹公讖四卷，劉向讖一卷，雜讖Documents二十九卷，堯戒舜、禹一卷，孔子王明鏡一卷，郭文金雄記一卷，王子年歌一卷，嵩高道士歌一卷。.
s1134.idiomatic: 孔老讖十二卷，老子河洛讖一卷，尹公讖四卷，劉向讖一卷，雜讖Documents二十九卷，堯戒舜、禹一卷，孔子王明鏡一卷，郭文金雄記一卷，王子年歌一卷，嵩高道士歌一卷。.

s1143.literal: 其Documents出於前漢，有河圖九篇，洛Documents六篇，雲自黃帝至周文王所受本文。.
s1143.idiomatic: 其Documents出於前漢，有河圖九篇，洛Documents六篇，雲自黃帝至周文王所受本文。.

s1146.literal: 而又有Documents中候、洛罪級、五行傳、Odes推度災、氾曆樞、含神務、孝經勾命訣、援神契、雜讖等Documents。.
s1146.idiomatic: 而又有Documents中候、洛罪級、五行傳、Odes推度災、氾曆樞、含神務、孝經勾命訣、援神契、雜讖等Documents。.

s1148.literal: 漢末，郎中郗萌集圖緯讖雜占為五十篇，謂之春秋災異。.
s1148.idiomatic: 漢末，郎中郗萌集圖緯讖雜占為五十篇，謂之春秋災異。.

s1167.literal: 秦相李斯作蒼頡篇，漢揚雄作訓纂篇，後漢郎中賈魴作滂喜篇，故曰三蒼。.
s1167.idiomatic: 秦相李斯作蒼頡篇，漢揚雄作訓纂篇，後漢郎中賈魴作滂喜篇，故曰三蒼。.

s1179.literal: 有司馬相如凡將篇，班固太甲篇、在昔篇，崔瑗飛龍篇，蔡邕聖皇篇、黃初篇、吳章篇，蔡邕女史篇，合八卷，又幼學二卷，硃育撰；.
s1179.idiomatic: 有司馬相如凡將篇，班固太甲篇、在昔篇，崔瑗飛龍篇，蔡邕聖皇篇、黃初篇、吳章篇，蔡邕女史篇，合八卷，又幼學二卷，硃育撰；.

s1323.literal: 魏世又有八分Documents，其字義訓讀，有史籀篇、蒼頡篇、三蒼、埤蒼、廣蒼等諸篇章，訓詁、說文字林、音義、聲韻、體勢等諸Documents。.
s1323.idiomatic: 魏世又有八分Documents，其字義訓讀，有史籀篇、蒼頡篇、三蒼、埤蒼、廣蒼等諸篇章，訓詁、說文字林、音義、聲韻、體勢等諸Documents。.
